city_tips.title: Use the Osaka Metro efficiently
city_tips.content: The Osaka Metro is Japan's second-most extensive metro network after Tokyo. Use the red Midosuji Line as the main artery connecting major attractions and districts. Keep your ticket to exit.
city_tips.evidence: The signage, ticketing and operation of the Osaka Metro are identical to its larger counterpart in Tokyo, and Tokyo's Pasmo/Suica smartcards are accepted as well.

city_tips.title: Try kuidaore, eat yourself into ruin
city_tips.content: Osaka is famous for its food culture. Experience authentic local cuisine at Dōtonbori with its countless restaurants serving okonomiyaki, takoyaki, and local specialties.
city_tips.evidence: The best place for trying out kuidaore is probably Dōtonbori (道頓堀) and neighboring Hōzenji-yokochō

city_tips.title: Osaka is remarkably safe for a major city
city_tips.content: While Osaka has a reputation for crime among Japanese residents, it remains extremely safe compared to Western cities of similar size. Avoid certain southern areas at night.
city_tips.evidence: Osaka has a reputation among the Japanese for being crime-ridden, but it is still remarkably safe compared to any Western city of similar size.

city_tips.title: Stand right on escalators to let others pass
city_tips.content: When using escalators, stand to the right to allow people in a hurry to pass on the left. This is the local custom in Osaka.
city_tips.evidence: When using escalators, stand to the right to allow people in a hurry to pass you on the left.

city_tips.title: Purchase transit passes for Kyoto travel
city_tips.content: Use Kyoto Sightseeing Cards (¥900 one-day, ¥1700 two-day) for unlimited subway and bus travel. Or purchase ICOCA card (¥2000) usable across Kansai region.
city_tips.evidence: The Kyoto Sightseeing Card can be purchased as a one-day (adults ¥900/children ¥450) or two-day pass (¥1700/¥850).

city_tips.title: Experience kaiseki and matcha specialties
city_tips.content: Kyoto is considered the spiritual home of kaiseki fine dining. Kyoto and nearby Uji are famous for matcha green tea and matcha-flavored treats.
city_tips.evidence: Kyoto is considered by most Japanese to be the spiritual home of kaiseki (懐石 or 会席), which is a meal of many small courses

city_tips.title: Spring and autumn offer best conditions
city_tips.content: Spring cherry blossoms and autumn colors are beautiful but crowded. Consider shoulder seasons for fewer tourists and pleasant weather.
city_tips.evidence: Kyoto is a major tourist destination, demand is high and prices follow suit. During peak seasons, such as the cherry blossoms in April or during Golden Week when accommodation is difficult to get
